/bin/zsh -c "cat > migration.test.sql <<'EOF'
-- Run with psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 against an empty test database.
\\ir schema.sql
INSERT INTO subscription VALUES ('old', '2024-06-01', '{\"monthlyFeeCents\":900}');
INSERT INTO pricing_history VALUES
  ('old', '2024-01-01', 900),
  ('old', '2024-07-01', 1500);
\\ir migration.sql
DO "'$$
BEGIN
  IF (SELECT fee_cents FROM pricing_decision WHERE subscription_id = '"'old') IS DISTINCT FROM 900 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Backfill did not use the price at approval';
  END IF;
  IF (SELECT terms->>'monthlyFeeCents' FROM subscription WHERE id = 'old') IS DISTINCT FROM '900' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Legacy terms were changed';
  END IF;
END "'$$;
EOF
docker exec fee-migration-check createdb -U postgres migration_test
cat schema.sql > /tmp/fee-schema.sql
# psql includes resolve on the container, so copy the fixture files there.
docker cp schema.sql fee-migration-check:/tmp/schema.sql
docker cp migration.sql fee-migration-check:/tmp/migration.sql
docker cp migration.test.sql fee-migration-check:/tmp/migration.test.sql
docker exec fee-migration-check psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d migration_test -f /tmp/migration.test.sql
docker rm -f fee-migration-check'

item.text:
Completed the pricing decision migration and next-version creation.

Existing subscriptions retain their legacy fee, while the migration records the price in force on the approval date. New versions omit the fee so it can be decided again. The migration reports negative fees and rolls back.

Checks passed: `bun test` and PostgreSQL 18 migration tests using pre-migration rows. A negative-fee check also confirmed that the migration fails and leaves the original subscription intact.
